videos.label: American Fork Police Detained Reckless Ben to “Scare” Him
The Cops Left One Fact Out of the Warrant. It Changes Everything | Reckless Ben Raid
videos.description: Brandon Grable compares the search warrant, probable-cause statement, and footage, and discusses the omitted civil-case verification and qualified immunity.

videos.label: American Fork Cops' own LEGO Scandal: They Raided Reckless Ben's Airbnb & Arrested Everyone
videos.description: Grable examines the Airbnb operation, handcuffing, transport to AFPD, and the grounds for detaining each occupant.

videos.label: Reckless Ben Saga: American Fork Police Training Records EXPOSED – No Immunity for the City
videos.description: Grable reviews released training records and discusses possible city liability. His legal conclusions are commentary; the released records may not represent every training an officer received.

videos.label: The Lego Raid Was Just the Beginning: American Fork PD’s Home Invasion Pattern
Interview with Civil Rights Attorney Taking On the American Fork Lego Raid
Cop Caught Saying "I Was Going to Scare Him" — Now American Fork Faces a Federal Lawsuit
videos.description: Commentary on the federal lawsuit filed by four people involved in the Reckless Ben encounters against American Fork and 13 officers. Discusses the complaint’s allegations; Ben Schneider is not a plaintiff.

videos.label: The Chief Admitted It in Private — The Plaintiffs Tell Their Side
videos.description: Daniel Sroka discusses his two meetings with Chief Cameron Paul about the March police encounters involving Reckless Ben and others. The video also features interviews with plaintiffs Sheldon Norcross and Steven Allen and their attorney, Solomon Radner.

videos.label: Chief Walked Back the LEGO Raid — Now the Transcript Is Out
videos.description: Brandon Grable reviews Daniel Sroka’s released transcript of his September 16 meeting with Chief Cameron Paul, with interview excerpts featuring Sroka, plaintiffs Steven Allen and Sheldon Norcross, and attorney Solomon Radner. Topics include the search warrant, transporting detainees, the phone seizure, body-camera gaps, redactions, and follow-up.
